content:
maya: Hey — noticed canary on text-gen-api is receiving ~38% of traffic even though rollout is 10% configured in Console. Seeing this since ~15:30 PDT. Console still shows 10% :thinking:

trent: Which route/path?

maya: POST /v1/generate (service=text-gen-api, environment=prod)

maya: Rollout snippet pasted:
```json
{
  "strategy": "weighted",
  "variants": [{"id": "stable", "weight": 90},{"id": "canary", "weight": 10}],
  "guards": [
    {"type": "cookie_affinity", "cookie_name": "rdw_session"},
    {"type": "header", "header": "x-redwood-canary", "value": "1"}
  ]
}
```

ops-bot: alert: rollout-drift detected for text-gen-api (configured 10% vs observed 38%)

li-chen: I pulled request logs. For requests without rdw_session cookie, a surprising portion are routing to the canary path. The routing decision log shows header guard matching even when header absent. Example routing trace:

```
EVALUATE GUARDS -> header:x-redwood-canary = null -> header-match: false
EVALUATE GUARDS -> cookie:rdw_session = null -> cookie-affinity: fallback -> assigned_variant: canary
```

li-chen: That "fallback -> assigned_variant: canary" line is weird — cookie-affinity fallback should go to stable per implementation.

maya: Hmm. I can reproduce with curl from staging:
```bash
curl -X POST https://prod.text-gen-api/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"hi"}' -v
```
Response headers show X-Assigned-Variant: canary on ~4/10 attempts.

trent: We shipped proxy header-normalization (lowercasing) two weeks ago. There was also a recent change that reorders guard evaluation to be "first match last-wins" for faster short-circuiting. I wonder if cookie_affinity was accidentally moved after header checks and the fallback logic uses the last-match variant instead of default stable.

li-chen: Confirmed in runtime: when cookie_affinity returns "no-cookie" we push a sentinel decision and continue; later header guard returns "no-match" but evaluation combines decisions and ends up picking the most recent non-null variant=canary because of a bug in mergeDecision().

maya: So two issues interacting: guard-order change + mergeDecision semantics. That explains why requests that should fall back to stable wind up at canary.

devex: Is the Console showing the same percent as actual backend? Could this be a telemetry-counting mismatch instead?

li-chen: Telemetry counts are fine — they count backend hits. The Console traffic summary queries routing_decision table which currently records the pre-merge guard hint (not the final backend assignment) in certain paths. So the UI can show 10% while backend receives ~38% because finalAssignment != recordedDecision for some requests.

trent: Proposed fix: (1) revert the guard-evaluation reordering so affinity guards run before header guards for rollouts, (2) change mergeDecision() to prefer explicit stable default on cookie fallback, and (3) update telemetry write to record finalAssignment only after merge. I'll put up a hotfix PR with tests.

maya: Thanks. Can you tag the PR? We should hotfix prod ASAP. This is customer-impacting (observed latency + weird model outputs).

trent: PR: github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4821 — patch includes unit tests and an e2e script to reproduce. Will request review from li-chen and ops.

li-chen: Reviewing now. Also adding a regression test that simulates cookie-less spike and asserts finalAssignment percentages match expected +/- 2%.

ops-bot: deploy: hotfix/rollout-guard-order -> prod triggered by trent at 2035678910

devex: Can we add a CanaryDrift alert in Console? When observed_pct - configured_pct > 15% fire. I’ll add it to the dashboard.

maya: Please also update runbook: if drift detected, check last 24h proxy commits and guard-eval reorderings.

li-chen: Patch LGTM. Hotfix will roll back the reordering and fix mergeDecision. I'll follow up with a postmortem and a test matrix for guard precedence permutations.

maya: :+1: Thanks everyone. Will monitor traffic and reopen if anything persists.

trent: I'll follow up with a short RFC to make guard precedence explicit (cookie-affinity -> sticky -> header -> metadata) and add telemetry hooks to assert recordedDecision === finalAssignment in CI.

ops-bot: deploy: completed successfully at 2035678914 :rocket:

maya: Verified: backend canary traffic dropped back to ~9.6% in the last 5 minutes. Closing for now, postmortem incoming. :white_check_mark:
